dish.title: Malaysian Curry Laksa with Shrimp
dish.description: A rich, spicy coconut noodle soup: a homemade paste of shallots, lemongrass, ginger, garlic, dried chiles, turmeric, and shrimp paste, sizzled in oil and simmered with coconut milk and stock, then poured over rice vermicelli and shrimp and piled with bean sprouts, cucumber, mint, and lime.

recipe_version.title: Malaysian Curry Laksa with Shrimp
recipe_version.description: A rich, spicy coconut noodle soup: a homemade paste of shallots, lemongrass, ginger, garlic, dried chiles, turmeric, and shrimp paste, sizzled in oil and simmered with coconut milk and stock, then poured over rice vermicelli and shrimp and piled with bean sprouts, cucumber, mint, and lime.

ingredients.name: dried red chiles
ingredients.display_name: dried red chiles (such as guajillo-size or Thai dried)

steps.title: Soak and blend the paste
steps.body: Pour 1 cup boiling water over the dried chiles and soak 15 minutes; drain and discard the soaking liquid. Meanwhile peel the shallots and garlic and chop the ginger and lemongrass. Blend the chiles, shallots, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, turmeric, coriander, and shrimp paste with 1 tbsp of the oil into a smooth paste. Cut the cucumber, pick the mint, and cut the limes. Put 16 cups (4 quarts) water on to boil for the noodles in the 6- to 8-quart pot.

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.body: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the 6-quart pot over medium. Cook the paste, stirring constantly, until it darkens, smells sweet, and the oil separates, 8 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.body: Whisk in the coconut milk and stock, add the fish sauce, brown sugar, and salt, and simmer on medium-low 12 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.body: While the broth simmers, cook the vermicelli in the 4 quarts of boiling water until tender, 3 to 4 minutes, and drain. Runs inside step 3 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Poach the shrimp
steps.body: Add the shrimp to the broth and simmer gently until pink, opaque, and firm, 3 to 4 minutes. Optional traditional preparation: shrimp that are still translucent in the center, about 120 F to 125 F. That lower temperature does not meet the USDA/FDA recommendation and carries higher risk, especially for young children, pregnant people, older adults, and anyone immunocompromised.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Divide the noodles and bean sprouts among deep bowls, ladle in the broth and shrimp, and top with cucumber, mint, and lime wedges.

equipment: second 6- to 8-quart pot for the noodles

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Unconditional dairy_free: the creaminess is coconut milk. Fish sauce is a seasoning, so the fish label is not used.
allergen_notes: Shellfish from the shrimp and shrimp paste (belacan).
Coconut is not a FlavorWeave allergen token; diners avoiding coconut should skip this dish.
Candlenuts (a common laksa paste ingredient) are omitted, so there are no tree nuts. No egg, milk, soy, wheat, sesame, or peanuts.

coverage_contribution: Malaysian 0 to 1. Adventurous complexity. A coconut noodle soup (the catalog's coconut dishes are curries and a fish stew).
near_duplicate_review: Compared with thai-red-curry-kabocha and coconut-chickpea-curry: a noodle soup with shrimp and homemade laksa paste, not a curry over rice. Compared with brazilian-fish-moqueca: Malaysian spice paste, noodles, shrimp. Compared with the burmese mohinga in this wave: coconut broth, shrimp, no chickpea thickener.
not_duplicate_of: Not tom kha. Not Sri Lankan fish curry (rejected).
